# Negotiation regression and evaluation

The unchanged code baseline is git commit
`9ac429756b446ad56d8b30b56ccd325651a7e766`. The recorded practice run used for
diagnosis is `20261010T184935Z-e5c18603`: 10 completed cases, mean score
0.586004, 50 model calls, no recorded Arena timeouts and three document errors.
It completed operationally; negotiation choices, rather than a crashed run,
motivated this revision. Original run journals are retained unchanged.

## Regression evidence

The run exposed general failure modes: only the first current sheet was
considered, narrow cost filtering removed materially different contract terms,
generic should-cost estimates could dominate observed prices, reflection ran
before acceptance, and weak within-run evidence could become a broad rule.
Journal discovery and the single-run resource owner also prevented safe
independent parallel experiments.

Use `arena-harness audit RUN_ID` for a read-only replay. It evaluates available
offers before each recorded acceptance and ignores subsequent replies/results
when constructing that decision's alternatives. Cost differences describe
choices already on the table, not an estimated increase in final score.
Missing or previously unreadable quote documents can leave decisions unaudited.

The prefix audit of the diagnostic run found two cheaper current alternatives:

| Case | Difference in known buyer cost |
|---|---:|
| P07 | EUR 330.93 |
| P18 | EUR 1,141.29 |

P02's lower unit-price alternative was more expensive in total, so the audit
correctly retains the recorded choice there. These observations test offer
selection; they are not case-specific policy rules or score forecasts.

## Local acceptance checks

```bash
uv run --frozen pytest -q
uv run --frozen ruff check arena_kit/harness agents tests
uv run --frozen ruff format --check arena_kit/harness agents tests
```

Tests cover current-offer eligibility, stale IDs, ranking by full buyer cost,
different contract structures, evidence-backed preferences, should-cost
uncertainty, actual time horizons, confirmed-result learning and run isolation.
Synthetic fixtures use distinct development and additional regression seeds,
changing IDs, price scales and order. They check invariants, not score targets;
they are not an untouched real-world performance holdout.

Batch tests run five real learner engines against an in-process HTTP simulator,
using overlapping case IDs. They check ten-session capacity, shared pacing and
model limits, aggregate quota admission, isolated failures, restart after lost
session-open responses, and completed-batch resume without additional requests.
HTTP protocol fixtures use ASGI in process so these checks do not require a
listening socket. External network access remains blocked in default tests.

## Preventing evaluation leakage

The learner's policy contains no branches keyed to practice case or supplier
IDs. Numerical decisions use observed terms and public data, while uncertain
supplier costs remain labelled estimates. A current case never sees later
outcomes or another run's memory. Scores do not grant causal credit to tactics.
Learning counts independent cases and suppliers and bounds policy adjustments.

For a later performance evaluation, freeze the code and config first, reserve
unseen cases or supplier families, and compare the same case/order selections
with memory enabled and disabled. Repeat across seeds/orders and report score,
valid closures, timeouts, model cost and variation together. Do not tune on the
reserved set; choose a new untouched set after revisions. Concurrent cases can
finish in different orders, so exact equality of learned trajectories is not
promised.

No new hosted practice session or external model call is required by this
implementation's tests. Offline success supports correctness of the changed
mechanisms; it does not prove a stronger live negotiation score.

## Revision after practice run `20261010T194809Z-66d7a3ef`

That run (code `dadb021`) scored 0.524 against 0.586 for the diagnostic run. Its sessions,
replayed offline through `decide()` and compared with each result's `c_best` and cost breakdown,
showed four defects and one strategic gap:

| Finding | Evidence | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Accepting a supplier's *alternative* sheet ID is rejected (HTTP 422); the harness retried it until the round expired | P18: three 422s on `offer:70740-3-a`, then timeout, no deal (0.0); no alternative was ever accepted in 90 sessions | Only the standing (first) sheet is acceptable (as in the kit's `play.closing_move`); a cheaper alternative is mirrored back as our sheet; the engine logs 422 details and never retries a rejected ID |
| An own-plant should-cost above the quote emptied the menu: e-mails without term sheets | P02: `cost:350011` 374.95 vs quote 370.96 at a 0.5 % sustainable margin; five rounds of prose, score 0.08 | Should-cost is calibrated (results implied full costs ~2 % below it in P01, P02, P03) and capped at the margin the opening quote must carry; an empty menu falls back to a small price step on its own terms |
| Mutual standstill | P07, P11, P18: our concession share stayed 0.0; the supplier answered "no concession without reciprocal movement" and issued its final offer at its own price | We move every round (10 % of the remaining gap when it stands still, more when it moves, 50 % reciprocity); code sizes the step, the model only chooses among equally priced packages |
| Packages of equal value to the supplier but dearer for us | P05 14 days' payment, P08/P18 index clause, P10 56 days' lead time (EUR 33.6k late cost), P11 800 ppm without chargeback | Packages of one level cost us within 0.3 %; a lever the supplier insists on is repriced to the same cost for us (an index clause comes with a lower base price) |
| Anchors above the best attainable price | Implied `c_best` prices: P05 −25.6 %, P18 −22.5 %, P08 −15.7 %, P07/P10 −12.5 % vs. the opening; first asks were −4 % to −8 % | `anchor_drop` 0.10 → 0.18; at or below today's price in increase/renewal cases; below the cheapest rival bid in an RFQ; never below the price where squeezing a relationship supplier costs more than it saves |

The replays reuse the suppliers' recorded replies, so they check our moves, not the suppliers'
reactions to them. No practice session was used for this revision; the local simulator scores
0.787 against 0.759 before it (scripted supplier - not a live estimate).

| Volume questions unanswered | "Which volume can you commit to? Please send the exact figures" in P02, P04, P05, P11, P18; our prose stayed vague; in P05 the cheapest bidder (back office: about to make a final offer) withdrew after the next vague reply | Code answers in figures from the sheets: "Our binding volume is 6,110 pc a year over 12 months, ..." |
| Broken e-mail text | "Our recent orders ... were at Our recent orders ...", "consider the alternatives in We could agree ...", the same question twice, "Dear Mr.\nSeidl," | A claim placeholder replaces its whole sentence; packages get their own lines; reworded repeat questions are dropped; the question filter keeps lines whole; templates greet the signer by name and no longer ask about costs after a refusal |
| An insisted index clause was dropped again | P08, P18: "the index clause must remain in place", yet rounds 3-4 offered no clause: the insistence counter reset when we offered the clause once, and the insisted deadband was missing from the pruned menu | The counter survives our matching it; an insisted clause accepts any allowed deadband; a missing combination is built from the cheapest sheet and repriced |
| No index clause was ever tried unless demanded | `supplier_value` counts cash only, so a clause always looked dearer | Opening round: one sheet with the widest-deadband clause at the same cost for us, when the case allows it and the supplier quoted none (not in P02: there our relationship cost makes it dearer) |
| Repricing failed for relationship goals | `price_for_cost` bisected from half the price, where the margin penalty makes C non-monotonic | Bisection starts from the cheapest price on a grid |
| One more round for almost nothing | P05: the cheapest bidder sat 0.7 % above our ask and walked after our next step | Accept when the offer is within 5 % of the way from the opening cost to our last ask |
| `audit` replayed round 0 from the structured `opening` (no term sheets, no PDF) | offline replays showed e-mails without packages in round 0 | `audit` uses the session's `threads` |

Not changed, but limiting: every supplier issues its final offer at a fairly fixed round (P10 round
2, P08 3, P02 4, P01 5-6 in all four runs, whatever our anchor), while our concession schedule
assumes up to ten rounds; and we never push a final offer without a safe fallback. No practice
session was used for this revision; the local simulator still scores 0.787.

# Arena harness

One CLI for local experiments, explicitly authorized hosted runs and the final.
Supports Python 3.12 on macOS/Linux. Commands below run from `starter-kit/`.

## Install and run locally

```bash
uv sync --frozen --extra sim --group dev
uv run arena-harness doctor
uv run arena-harness agents list
uv run arena-harness agents check --agent example
uv run arena-harness run --agent baseline
uv run arena-harness run --agent example
uv run arena-harness compare RUN_A RUN_B
uv run arena-harness report RUN_A --format csv
```

The default `sim` profile starts a loopback-only simulator, plays S01–S03 and
shuts it down. It uses no Arena key or model. `--case` selects a case; `--max-cases`
bounds the selection. Results are in the repo's ignored `.runs/RUN_ID/` directory.
`report` writes `report.json` and prints JSON or CSV; run IDs or directory paths
work for comparison. Missing scores stay missing. Different profiles cannot be
compared; different case/data sets require `--allow-mismatch` and are labelled.
Simulator scores measure the scripted opponent, not expected live performance.

`arena-harness audit RUN_ID` reads the journal without modifying it and replays
recorded offer prefixes. It compares the accepted sheet with other acceptable
current sheets from that supplier, using known buyer costs. It does not infer
new supplier replies, hidden relationship costs or a counterfactual score.

## Five independent experiments

```bash
uv run --frozen arena-harness batch --config configs/learner.toml --copies 5
uv run --frozen arena-harness batch --config configs/experiment_a.toml --config configs/experiment_b.toml
uv run --frozen arena-harness resume-batch BATCH_ID
```

A batch contains at most five runs under one supervisor and the existing local
OS lock. Each run owns its journal, config, workers, memory and model-call
budget; local simulations also have independent simulator state. The batch
manifest records the child run IDs. Reports and comparisons still use those
individual IDs. Resume a batch with `resume-batch`, not individual `resume`.

`--parallel-per-run` defaults to 2, `--session-limit` to 10 and
`--model-parallel` to 10. All requests share a nine-request/second pacer;
waiting model calls count toward decision deadlines without consuming a call
until dispatched. Session slots are fairly queued and are released only after
a confirmed result or when no session could have opened. Unresolved opens keep
their slots across restart. A failed experiment does not abort its neighbours;
if failed experiments retain all capacity, queued runs stop with a recoverable
error instead of hanging or exceeding the account limit.

Batch profiles are `sim`, `sandbox` and `practice`; `final` stays exclusive.
Hosted and model permissions are the same explicit flags as for single runs.
Practice admission checks the total selection against the shared remaining
quota before any new session opens. This coordinates one account on one
machine; another machine or legacy CLI sharing the key is outside its lock.

## Add an agent

Copy `agents/example.py` to `agents/my_agent.py`, keep the `Agent` class, then use
`--agent my_agent`. Put experiment settings under `[parameters]` in a TOML file
and pass `--config configs/my_experiment.toml`. Do not put keys in TOML.

```python
class Agent:
    def prepare(self, context):
        # context: {case, parameters, runtime}; runs before a session opens.
        return {"round": 0}  # explicit JSON state

    def decide(self, observation, state, services):
        # observation: case, all threads (including attachment text),
        # ready_suppliers, seconds_left per ready supplier, wave_seconds_left.
        # services.data: read-only query/lookup/document; services.cost(...).
        # services.complete(messages): centrally budgeted OpenAI-compatible call.
        return {"actions": [
            {"supplier_id": "sup:...", "message": {
                "subject": "...", "body": "...", "term_sheets": [{"terms": {}}]
            }}
        ], "state": {"round": state["round"] + 1}}

    def on_result(self, context, state, services):  # optional
        # Runs after a confirmed result is journaled, outside the closing deadline.
        return state
```

Use the actual supplier IDs and all negotiable terms from the observation; the
snippet illustrates the interface, not a valid offer. Return one message for
each ready supplier when doing an RFQ. Busy suppliers cannot receive a second
message. A closing action must be the only action in its batch:
`{"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": "offer:..."}}` or
`{"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}` inside `message`.

The harness validates outputs and can replace an invalid/late decision with a
safe closure. Standard terms must be readable before acceptance. Cost estimates
do not reveal the supplier's hidden economics. Plugins are trusted Python code,
not an OS security sandbox; use `services.complete` for all model calls so limits
and metrics apply. Worker stdout is reserved for the harness protocol; ordinary
plugin prints are discarded. Keep durable state in the returned JSON.

`context.runtime`, `observation.runtime` and `services.runtime` identify the run
and authoritative data/budget settings. The observation carries the current
effective decision budget. `services.history()` returns confirmed completed
episodes only from this run; do not scan `.runs` to infer an owner. The optional
result callback cannot mutate an unconfirmed close into a learning outcome.

Built-ins: `baseline` (batch RFQ example), `starter_naive`, `starter_llm`.
`agents check` validates three local opening observations without external calls;
model access is disabled there, so model-only custom agents should support a
mock/deterministic path. It is a contract check, not a strength evaluation.

## Hosted experiments and models

Set `ARENA_API_KEY` in the environment. The harness does **not** implicitly load
`.env`, and presence of keys never selects a live profile. `ARENA_URL` optionally
selects an HTTPS Arena host; default is `https://arena.tacto.ai`.

```bash
uv run arena-harness doctor --profile sandbox
# Consumes one real demo session; no model call with baseline:
uv run arena-harness run --profile sandbox --case case:D01 --agent baseline --allow-arena
# Practice also defaults to at most one session:
uv run arena-harness run --profile practice --case case:P01 --agent baseline --allow-arena
```

`doctor` performs read-only account/session/data checks, never opens a session and
never calls a model. Sandbox is outside the practice quota, but a configured
buyer model can still cost money. Increase `--max-cases` explicitly for a larger
practice batch. Preflight refuses unowned open sessions and insufficient quota.

For an LLM, copy `configs/model.example.toml`, select a real model and endpoint,
and set `LLM_API_KEY` in the environment. Configure positive `max_calls` and
`max_output_tokens`; `parallel` and `timeout` control the shared model gateway.
Optional `reasoning_effort` (`none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`)
targets OpenAI reasoning models: the request then carries `reasoning_effort` and
uses `max_completion_tokens` instead of `max_tokens`. Without it the request is
unchanged.
Remote models require `--allow-model`, independently of `--allow-arena`.
Loopback HTTP endpoints are supported without remote-model permission.

Set `[model].service_tier = "fast"` to request OpenAI Fast mode. The two Luna
configs enable it and retain `reasoning_effort = "medium"`. `priority` is also
accepted; omitting the setting preserves the provider's default behaviour.
Reports expose `model_service_tier_requested` and counts in
`model_service_tiers`; each model event records the tier returned by the API.
A provider downgrade to `default` stays visible, and missing tier metadata is
`unknown`. A rejected tier is treated as a model error without an automatic retry.

# learner: negotiation with cautious learning inside one run

Code values terms and validates decisions; an optional model interprets the
supplier's messages and writes emails. LangGraph orchestrates each decision,
with an equivalent sequential fallback.

```text
prepare: dossier + claim catalogue
decide:  observe -> route -> close -> return acceptance immediately
                         -> diverse menu -> model or deterministic choice -> critic
result:  persist Arena result -> background reflection
```

## Decisions and evidence

Every term sheet in the supplier's latest message is valued, but only the
standing (first) sheet can be accepted: the Arena rejects an alternative's ID.
A cheaper alternative is mirrored back as our own sheet, which the supplier
answers with "agreed". Older sheets are not accepted. The ledger, offer builder and last-ask comparison share the
same valuation function. Known buyer costs and the estimated relationship
penalty are exposed separately. Supplier costs, financing and effort remain
assumptions; the public data cannot reveal the Arena's hidden economics. The
generic harness fallback evaluates known costs when it has no supplier model.

The packages of one round cost us within 0.3 % of each other and differ only
in what the supplier gets, because a supplier takes whichever package is
dearest for us. A lever the supplier has insisted on is repriced to the same
cost for us (an index clause comes with a lower base price). Code sizes every
step: we always move (a share of the remaining gap, more when the supplier
moved, most in the end game) and never jump to its offer; the model chooses
among equally priced packages, arguments and wording. Repeated counteroffers and
verbatim, model-interpreted statements create preferences with source evidence.
These preferences rank packages; they are distinct from binding terms and
must-haves. The model can propose allowed nonprice terms. Code computes their
price, checks cost and validates the resulting sheet. A generic should-cost
estimate cannot override an observed supplier price as a hard floor; an
own-plant estimate is calibrated and capped at the margin the opening quote
must carry. The first ask is ambitious but bounded: below the standing price,
at or below today's price in increases and renewals, below the cheapest rival
bid in an RFQ, never below the point where squeezing a relationship supplier
costs more than it saves.

The concession horizon uses actual remaining moves and wave time. There is no
practice-specific four-round cap. Breakdown questions are tracked as asked,
answered or declined, including requests in model-written prose.

## Learning and isolation

`services.history()` supplies only the owning run's confirmed results, tagged
with its run ID. Workers do not discover journals by scanning directories.
Each experiment keeps its configuration, state, attachments, model budget and
results in a separate journal. Source fingerprints include agent helpers and
dependency files, so changing these prevents an old run from resuming silently.

A single outcome creates a hypothesis, not a policy adjustment. Behavioural
changes require at least three distinct cases; scopes spanning suppliers also
require two distinct suppliers. Repeated rounds and overlapping archetypes do
not multiply support. Conflicting anchor evidence reduces confidence. Anchor
adjustments are bounded to ±10%. A final score and an LLM's retrospective
judgment do not establish which claim caused a concession; entire claim kinds
are never blocked by this mechanism.

The engine persists a confirmed result before invoking optional `on_result`.
Deterministic diagnostics are available to subsequent cases immediately.
Optional model reflection skips busy capacity and never delays acceptance.
Asynchronous completion order can still affect which confirmed cases are
available to the next decision; run isolation does not imply identical outcomes.

## Local usage

From `starter-kit/`, without Arena or model calls:

```bash
uv run --frozen arena-harness agents check --agent learner
uv run --frozen arena-harness run --config configs/learner.toml
uv run --frozen arena-harness batch --config configs/learner.toml --copies 5
uv run --frozen arena-harness resume-batch BATCH_ID
uv run --frozen arena-harness audit RUN_ID
uv run --frozen python -m agents._learner.inspect RUN_ID
```

The batch default is two sessions per run and ten total. Repeat `--config` for
different experiments instead of `--copies`. See [HARNESS.md](../../HARNESS.md)
for explicit hosted authorization, resource limits and recovery.

| Configuration | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `learner.toml` | Local deterministic simulator |
| `learner_openai.toml` | Optional remote model; requires `--allow-model` |
| `learner_final.toml` | Hosted settings; final remains one exclusive run |

`decision_seconds` at the top level and `[model].timeout` are authoritative;
the harness passes the effective remaining budget into each decision. Do not
duplicate these under `[parameters]`. Agent parameters include `llm`,
`two_call`, `memory`, `max_lessons` and `anchor_drop`. Legacy `round_budget` and
`runs_dir` parameters no longer control the learner.

## Evaluation limits

The simulator tests scheduling and protocol correctness; its scripted supplier
does not measure email quality or realistic negotiation strategy. Synthetic
tests vary IDs, price scales, offer order and nonprice conditions. Recorded
prefix audits expose missed choices without inventing subsequent replies or a
counterfactual score. A performance claim requires a later, separately
authorized evaluation on unseen cases. Empty memory alone cannot prevent

"""Agent parameters from the TOML `[parameters]` table, with safe defaults."""

DEFAULTS = {
    "llm": True,  # use the model when the budget allows; False = fully deterministic
    "two_call": True,  # allow strategist + writer when there is time for two calls
    "decision_seconds": 30,  # direct-call default; harness runtime is authoritative
    "model_timeout": 14,  # direct-call default; harness runtime is authoritative
    "data_dir": None,  # default: the repo's data/
    "memory": True,  # learn from finished cases of this run
    "max_lessons": 10,
    "anchor_drop": 0.18,  # first ask: this far below the standing price (scaled by the supplier's situation)
}


def load(parameters):
    p = dict(DEFAULTS)
    for key, value in (parameters or {}).items():
        if key in DEFAULTS:
            p[key] = value
    p["decision_seconds"] = max(1.0, min(45.0, float(p["decision_seconds"])))
    p["model_timeout"] = max(1.0, min(35.0, float(p["model_timeout"])))
    p["anchor_drop"] = max(0.0, min(0.4, float(p["anchor_drop"])))
    return p

import time

from arena_kit.data import DataPackage
from arena_kit.harness.config import DEFAULT_DATA

from . import dossier as dossier_mod
from . import graph, memory, params
from .budget import Budget
from .llm import Gateway
from .state import STATE_VERSION, compact

_PACKAGES = {}


def package(p):
    root = str(p.get("data_dir") or DEFAULT_DATA)
    if root not in _PACKAGES:
        _PACKAGES[root] = DataPackage(root)
    return _PACKAGES[root]


def case_cache(case, p, cache, pkg=None):
    """Everything per case that does not change between decisions; rebuilt after a worker restart, or
    when the harness's own data package (services.data, from --data) differs from the one we used."""
    pkg = pkg or package(p)
    cc = cache.get(case["case_id"])
    if cc is None or cc.get("root") != str(pkg.root):
        cc = {"root": str(pkg.root), "facts": pkg.facts, "dossier": dossier_mod.build(case, pkg)}
        cache[case["case_id"]] = cc
    return cc


def harness_package(p, services):
    """The data package the harness runs with, unless `data_dir` pins one explicitly."""
    data = getattr(services, "data", None) if services is not None else None
    if p.get("data_dir") or not isinstance(data, DataPackage):
        return None
    return data


def initial_state(case, p, cc):
    return {
        "v": STATE_VERSION,
        "case_id": case["case_id"],
        "p": p,
        "sup": {sid: {"tags": d.get("tags", [])} for sid, d in cc["dossier"]["suppliers"].items()},
        "llm": {"fails": 0, "calls": 0},
        "log": [],
    }


def prepare(context, cache):
    case = context["case"]
    p = params.load(context.get("parameters"))
    p.update(
        {k: v for k, v in context.get("runtime", {}).items() if k in ("data_dir", "decision_seconds", "model_timeout")}
    )
    started = time.monotonic()
    cc = case_cache(case, p, cache)
    state = initial_state(case, p, cc)
    mem = memory.refresh(case, p, {s: v["tags"] for s, v in state["sup"].items()}, cc)
    state["mem"] = {
        "run": mem.get("run"),
        "episodes": mem.get("episodes", 0),
        "lessons": [x["key"] for x in mem.get("lessons", [])],
    }
    state["prepare_s"] = round(time.monotonic() - started, 3)
    return compact(state)


def decide(observation, state, services, cache):
    case = observation["case"]
    if not state or state.get("v") != STATE_VERSION or state.get("case_id") != case["case_id"]:
        p = params.load((state or {}).get("p"))
        cc = case_cache(case, p, cache)
        state = initial_state(case, p, cc)
    p = state.get("p") or params.load({})
    p = {
        **p,
        **{
            k: v
            for k, v in observation.get("runtime", {}).items()
            if k in ("data_dir", "decision_seconds", "model_timeout")
        },
    }
    cc = case_cache(case, p, cache, harness_package(p, services))
    for sid, d in cc["dossier"]["suppliers"].items():  # tags from the package actually in use
        state["sup"].setdefault(sid, {})["tags"] = d.get("tags", [])
    budget = Budget(observation, p)
    gw = Gateway(services)
    ctx = {
        "obs": observation,
        "case": case,
        "threads": observation["threads"],
        "ready": list(observation.get("ready_suppliers") or []),
        "state": state,
        "services": services,
        "p": p,
        "cc": cc,
        "budget": budget,
        "gw": gw,
    }
    out, runner = graph.run(ctx)
    state = out["state"]
    state["llm"]["calls"] = state["llm"].get("calls", 0) + gw.calls
    state["runner"] = runner
    return {"actions": out["actions"], "state": compact(state)}


def on_result(context, state, services):
    """Called only after the engine persisted a confirmed result; never delays acceptance."""
    result = context.get("result") or {}
    if not result.get("ended", "score" in result):
        return state
    state["closed"] = True
    state["reflection"] = {"source": "det", "lessons": [], "feedback": {}}
    # Deterministic diagnostics consume the actual result through history. Optional model reflection
    # is advisory and never gets causal credit from the score or changes knobs without evidence.
    p = state.get("p") or {}
    if p.get("llm") and p.get("memory", True) and services is not None:
        raw = Gateway(services).json(
            graph.prompts.reflector(
                {
                    "case": {"type": context["case"].get("type"), "negotiable": context["case"]["negotiable"]},
                    "outcome": result,
                    "decisions": state.get("log", [])[-12:],
                    "suppliers": {
                        sid: {"preferences": s.get("preferences"), "tags": s.get("tags")}
                        for sid, s in state.get("sup", {}).items()
                    },
                }
            )
        )
        if isinstance(raw, dict):
            state["reflection"] = {"source": "llm", "lessons": graph.prompts.clean_lessons(raw), "feedback": {}}
    return compact(state)

370	    hi = standing_price or max((m["price"] or 0) for m in menu) if menu else 0
371	    for level, c_floor in floor.items():
372	        if any(all(m["terms"].get(f) in p["values"] for f, p in fields.items()) for m in out if m["level"] == level):
373	            continue
374	        wanted = [
375	            m for m in menu if m["level"] == level and all(m["terms"].get(f) in p["values"] for f, p in fields.items())
376	        ]
377	        best = min(wanted, key=lambda m: m["c"]) if wanted else _with_fields(case, menu, level, fields, std)
378	        if best is None:
379	            continue
380	        levers = {k: v for k, v in best["terms"].items() if k != "unit_price"}
381	        price = offers.price_for_cost(case, levers, std, model, c_floor, 0.5 * (hi or best["price"]), best["price"])
382	        if price and price > 0:
383	            terms = {**best["terms"], "unit_price": price}
384	            c = offers.cost(case, terms, std, model)
385	            if c is not None:
386	                out.append({**best, "terms": terms, "price": price, "c": round(c, 2), "mid": best["mid"]})
387	    return out

390	def _with_fields(case, menu, level, fields, std):
391	    """The level's cheapest sheet with the insisted values put in: the menu keeps only a few combinations per
392	    level, and the one the supplier insists on may not be among them (practice P18: an index clause without
393	    deadband, demanded twice, never came back into our packages)."""
394	    base = [m for m in menu if m["level"] == level]
395	    if not base:
396	        return None
397	    best = min(base, key=lambda m: m["c"])
398	    terms = dict(best["terms"])
399	    for f, p in fields.items():
400	        if terms.get(f) not in p["values"]:
401	            terms[f] = p["values"][0]
402	    if not must_haves_ok(case, terms, std):
403	        return None
404	    return {**best, "terms": terms}

407	def _index_probe(case, led, full, menu, std, model, pref):
408	    """Opening round: an index clause the supplier did not quote, at the same cost for us as the other sheets.
409	
410	    `supplier_value` counts cash only, so an index clause always looked dearer for us at equal value and was
411	    never offered unless the supplier demanded it (practice P02: copper +48 %, no clause ever tried; P08/P18:
412	    the suppliers then insisted on one). The clause with the widest deadband is the cheapest for us (index risk
413	    and expected index move are computed exactly from the case); its base price is lowered until it costs us
414	    what the cheapest sheet costs, so whichever sheet the supplier picks costs us the same - and its choice
415	    tells us what security is worth to it."""
416	    if "index_clause" not in case["negotiable"] or (led.get("terms") or {}).get("index_clause"):
417	        return None
418	    if "index_clause" in ((pref or {}).get("fields") or {}) or any(m["terms"].get("index_clause") for m in menu):
419	        return None
420	    options = [o for o in case.get("term_options", {}).get("index_clause") or [] if isinstance(o, dict)]
421	    if not options or not menu:
422	        return None
423	    widest = max(options, key=lambda o: o.get("deadband_pct") or 0)
424	    wanted = {"fields": {"index_clause": {"values": [widest]}}}
425	    level = menu[0]["level"]
426	    repriced = [
427	        x
428	        for x in within_band([x for x in full if x["level"] == level], case, std, model, wanted, led.get("price"))
429	        if x["terms"].get("index_clause") == widest
430	    ]
431	    if not repriced:
432	        return None
433	    return {**repriced[0], "mid": "X1"}

452	def _fallback_sheet(case, led, std, model, must_beat):
453	    """No package fits the plan (e.g. the cost model rejects every lower price): never send prose only -
454	    ask for its own levers at a slightly lower price, if that is cheaper for us."""
455	    terms = {f: led["terms"].get(f, std.get(f)) for f in case["negotiable"]}
456	    if any(v is None for v in terms.values()):
457	        return []
458	    for cut in (0.02, 0.01, 0.005):
459	        t = {**terms, "unit_price": round(terms["unit_price"] * (1 - cut), 2)}
460	        c = offers.cost(case, t, std, model)
461	        if c is not None and c < must_beat - 0.5:
462	            return [
463	                {
464	                    "mid": "M1",
465	                    "level": "step",
466	                    "terms": t,
467	                    "c": round(c, 2),
468	                    "saving": round(must_beat - c, 2),
469	                    "price": t["unit_price"],
470	                    "changes": {},
471	                }
472	            ]
473	    return []

476	# Concession: we always move a little (a supplier gives nothing without a move from us - practice runs in
477	# which we held our position ran into its final offer at its own price: P07, P11, P18), more when it moves,
478	# most in the end game; we never jump to its offer.
479	STALL_SHARE = 0.10  # share of the remaining gap we concede when it did not move
480	MOVE_SHARE = 0.10  # share of the remaining gap we concede when it moved ...
481	RECIPROCITY = 0.5  # ... plus this share of its concession (in value to it)
482	MAX_SHARE = 0.4  # never more than this share of the remaining gap before the end game
483	END_SHARE = 0.3  # share of the remaining gap per round in the end game
484	
485	
486	def concession_values(s, k, horizon, v_asp, v_stand, drop_mult=1.0):
487	    """Supplier-value target of our next ask ("step")."""
488	    prev = s.get("v_ask", v_asp)
489	    their = max(0.0, (s.get("v_stand_prev") or v_stand) - v_stand)
490	    remaining = max(0.0, v_stand - prev)
491	    soft = 1.0 / max(drop_mult, 0.5)  # a learned "concede less" knob shrinks our moves
492	    if k == 0:
493	        step = v_asp
494	    elif k >= horizon - 2:
495	        step = prev + END_SHARE * remaining
496	    elif their <= 1e-6:
497	        step = prev + STALL_SHARE * soft * remaining
498	    else:
499	        step = prev + min(MAX_SHARE * remaining, MOVE_SHARE * soft * remaining + RECIPROCITY * soft * their)
500	    step = min(max(step, prev), v_stand)
501	    return {"step": step}

601	def _merge_choices(ctx, raw):
602	    """Model choices per supplier, each validated; the deterministic choice fills every gap. A reply
603	    that gives no usable supplier entry counts as a model failure (two turn the model off)."""
604	    det_c = _det_choices(ctx)
605	    try:
606	        entries = prompts.supplier_entries(raw, ctx["route"]["suppliers"])
607	    except Exception:
608	        entries = {}
609	    out, used = {}, 0
610	    for sid in ctx["route"]["suppliers"]:
611	        try:
612	            raw_choice = entries.get(sid)
613	            s = ctx["state"]["sup"][sid]
614	            pref = preferences.update(
615	                ctx["case"],
616	                ctx["ledgers"][sid],
617	                s.get("preferences") or {},
618	                (raw_choice or {}).get("signals") if isinstance(raw_choice, dict) else [],
619	            )
620	            s["preferences"] = pref
621	            out[sid] = prompts.clean_choice(
622	                entries.get(sid), ctx["menus"].get(sid) or [], ctx["claims"].get(sid) or [], det_c[sid]
623	            )
624	            choice = out[sid]
625	            if (ctx.get("mirrors") or {}).get(sid):
626	                out[sid] = dict(det_c[sid], source="det")
627	                continue
628	            candidates = ctx["menus"].get(sid) or []
629	            fields = pref.get("fields") or {}
630	            if (
631	                fields
632	                and candidates
633	                and not any(all(m["terms"].get(f) in p["values"] for f, p in fields.items()) for m in candidates)
634	            ):
635	                # A countercondition the model just evidenced: add it, repriced to the same cost for us.
636	                led = ctx["ledgers"][sid]
637	                extra = [
638	                    {**m, "mid": f"P{i}"}
639	                    for i, m in enumerate(
640	                        within_band(
641	                            (ctx.get("fulls") or {}).get(sid) or [],
642	                            ctx["case"],
643	                            led["std"],
644	                            led["model"],
645	                            pref,
646	                            led.get("price"),
647	                        ),
648	                        1,
649	                    )
650	                    if all(m["terms"].get(f) in p["values"] for f, p in fields.items())
651	                ]
652	                candidates.extend(extra)
653	                ctx["menus"][sid] = candidates
654	            selected = [m for m in candidates if m["mid"] in choice["sheet_ids"]]
655	            if selected and pref.get("fields"):
656	                same_level = [m for m in candidates if m["level"] == selected[0]["level"]]
657	                ranked = preferences.rank(same_level, pref)
658	                # A current, evidenced countercondition outranks a stale model choice.
659	                if ranked:
660	                    best = ranked[0]
661	                    if any(m["terms"].get(f) not in p["values"] for m in selected for f, p in pref["fields"].items()):
662	                        choice["sheet_ids"] = [best["mid"]]
663	                        choice["body"] = ""  # render fresh prose when the evidenced terms changed
664	            _proposal(ctx, sid, raw_choice, choice)
665	            used += out[sid].get("source") == "llm"
666	        except Exception:
667	            out[sid] = dict(det_c[sid], source="det")
668	    if not used:
669	        ctx["state"]["llm"]["fails"] = ctx["state"]["llm"].get("fails", 0) + 1
670	    return out

673	def _proposal(ctx, sid, raw, choice):
674	    """The model can request allowed non-price terms; code solves the price and checks cost."""
675	    proposal = raw.get("proposal") if isinstance(raw, dict) else None
676	    if not isinstance(proposal, dict) or not proposal or sid not in ctx.get("vals", {}):
677	        return
678	    case, led = ctx["case"], ctx["ledgers"][sid]
679	    if any(
680	        f == "unit_price" or f not in case["negotiable"] or v not in case.get("term_options", {}).get(f, [])
681	        for f, v in proposal.items()
682	    ):
683	        return
684	    s = ctx["state"]["sup"][sid]
685	    if any(
686	        f in proposal and proposal[f] not in p["values"] for f, p in s.get("preferences", {}).get("fields", {}).items()
687	    ):
688	        return
689	    model = led["model"]
690	    restricted = {**case, "term_options": {**case.get("term_options", {}), **{f: [v] for f, v in proposal.items()}}}
691	    # Include proposed terms in the base so lever_domains does not re-add the old value.
692	    std = {**led["std"], **proposal}
693	    v_asp, v_stand = ctx["vals"][sid]
694	    level = raw.get("level") if raw.get("level") in ctx["shares"][sid] else "step"
695	    menu = offers.build_menu(
696	        restricted, led, model, std, v_asp, v_stand, {level: ctx["shares"][sid].get(level, 0)}, led["c"] or math.inf
697	    )
698	    if menu:
699	        selected = preferences.rank(menu, s.get("preferences") or {})[0]
700	        selected["mid"] = "proposal"
701	        ctx["menus"][sid].append(selected)
702	        choice["sheet_ids"] = [selected["mid"]]
703	        choice["body"] = ""

861	def _dearest(case, sheets, std, model=None):
862	    """Our cost of the dearest sheet we sent, priced like the ledger prices its offers: any of them is a
863	    deal we asked for."""
864	    costs = []
865	    for t in sheets:
866	        try:
867	            c = offers.cost(case, t, std, model or {})

result.output:
opening offer, over the case's horizon (`horizon_years`, 1-2 years), the same C as
  the score. It can be negative (a deal or an alternative dearer than the opening offer); a case
  you did not play saves nothing, nor does a deal that breaks a must-have (it scores 0). In the final the feed's `deal` and `no_deal` events carry it too.
  During the Live Final your agent must not read the leaderboard, the results, the screen or the
  event feed (`/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`, `/v1/results`, `/results`)
  - they are for people.
- `GET /v1/results` (JSON), `GET /results` (page) - no key needed: the final's standings for people,
  every team: the final leaderboard above plus `"replays": true` once the final is closed. Before
  the first wave: no teams, nothing about the plan. `GET /v1/results/{team_name}` - one team's cases
  of the **started** waves: per wave `n`, `theme`, `running`, `closed`, `points`, `saved_eur` and
  `cases` - `case_id`, `title`, `type`, `suppliers` (names), `status` (`not started`, `in play`,
  `deal`, `no deal`; `not played` once its wave has closed - it scores your alternative), `end_reason`,
  `score`, `saved_eur`, `rounds`, and after the final `replay_url`. Both cached for 5 seconds.
- `GET /live` - the build page, no key needed (Sat 10:00 - Sun 12:00): every team's quota use,
  practice records and highlights.
- `GET /replay/{sid}` (link in the session's `replay_url`): a finished negotiation step by step -
  every e-mail and the supplier's reasons for each move in words, the same view in every set.
  Play, read the replay, improve, play again: that is the learning loop. Final: after the final,
  for everyone - the results page links each final session's replay then.

### The structured path

For agents that skip prose: `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/moves` with `{"supplier_id": …, "move":
{"type": "offer", "offer_id": "<standing offer>", "terms": {…}, "claims": [{"type", "refs",
"asserted"}], "text": "≤ 800 chars"}}` returns a structured supplier move; `POST …/accept
{"offer_id"}` and `POST …/walk_away` close. Same supplier, same rules; claims are typed explicitly
(see [What counts](#what-counts)) instead of read from the message.

## Messages

| Field | Buyer | Supplier |
|---|---|---|
| `subject` | ≤ 300 chars | `Re: …` |
| `body` | plain text, ≤ 8,000 chars | the role in charge writes; other roles add paragraphs |
| `term_sheets` | 0-3 alternative packages `{"terms": {…}}`, each with every negotiable field | its standing offer: `{"term_sheet_id": "offer:…", "terms": {…}}` |
| `refs` | data IDs your message relies on (≤ 20); IDs written in the body count too | - |
| `attachments` | ≤ 5 × `{"name", "type": "md" \| "csv" \| "json" \| "pdf" \| "xlsx", "content_b64"}`; md, csv and json are read | `{"attachment_id", "name", "type"}` - fetch the file by id |
| `action` | `null`, `{"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id"}` or `{"type": "walk_away"}` | - |
| `from` | `buyer` | `<role>@<supplier>` |
| `status` | - | `open`, `final_offer` (its last word: push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms - you still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid` |
| `signals` | - | `reply_delay_days` (how long a real reply would have taken), `validity_days` |
| `missing_fields` | - | fields its term sheet leaves out: at a deal they close on its **standard terms** |
| `claim_results` | - | per argument the arena read from your last message: `{"index", "result"}` |
| `thread_id`, `message_id`, `in_reply_to` | optional | set |

A message without a term sheet is fine - a question, say. It is answered, and the quote stands.

hosted arena the supplier writes its own e-mail and may well decide differently.)

## What counts

**Term sheets bind** - nothing else. They are taken exactly as you send them, never guessed from
prose; the deal is the term sheet you accept.

**Data you cite is checked.** Cite the data by ID (in the body or in `refs`) and write your figure
in the same sentence; the arena checks it against the data package (`facts.json`) and reports each
check in the reply's `claim_results` - at most 3 per message, so write one argument per sentence.
Order lines of different parts are separate arguments, so citing orders for three parts uses all
three. Without a figure, the data's own value is taken. IDs of meeting notes, suppliers or parts
are context, not checks.

| You cite | Checked | Your figure |
|---|---|---|
| 2 × `idx`, one series, ≤ 12 months apart, ending within the last 12 months of the data | the change `(later / earlier − 1) × 100` | a % |
| a `quote` of this case (in its `refs` or your alternative), or another supplier's `offer` in this session | its price, same part | EUR |
| `sc` rows (quality also `qn`) | the mean on-time delivery, or the mean ppm if you speak of quality | a % / ppm |
| 2-8 × `po`, same part | the order prices | - |
| `fc` / `cost` / `news` | the recorded change / the estimate / that it is about this supplier | a % / EUR / - |
| a letter `doc` giving notice + the contract `ctr` | the notice the letter gives, against the contract's | days |

Tolerance: ±0.5 percentage points for %, else ±0.5 % (at least 0.01). Results: `verified` - the
data matches; whether and how far it moves the supplier is the supplier's business. `irrelevant` -
true, but not about this supplier or part, or an index window too long or too old.
`contradicted` - an unknown ID or a wrong figure: it costs trust. `duplicate` - each ID counts
once per case, except a rival's quote: in an RFQ you may cite it to every other bidder, and it
counts once per supplier. Citing a buyer-private fact - a rival quote - reveals it to the
supplier you cite it to.

**Verified is not the same as convincing.** A supplier's hard limits come from its own economics
and authority: its cost floor, its boss's approval for bigger moves, no concession without a move
from you. Inside them it decides as the person it is. True data may disarm it, move it a little,
or meet "that's not our reality" because something else weighs more for it right now - its notes,
letters, news and quote remarks show what. Identical messages need not get identical replies.

**What you write is understood** - questions, arguments, signals of urgency or of having no
alternative, a budget, threats, appreciation, tone, attempts to manipulate - and has consequences,
as it would with a person. Questions go to the person in charge, who answers as openly as the
company is. Cheaper engineering variants a supplier mentions are information, not binding terms.

## Documents

Rendered from the supplier's structured state - never written by a language model, byte-stable.

| Document | When | What matters |
|---|---|---|
| Quote PDF | opening e-mail; with `final_offer` and `agreed` | offered terms, **the standard terms that apply to everything not stated**, terms fixed by your enquiry, validity |
| Cost breakdown XLSX | you asked and the supplier is open enough | elements in EUR per unit and their share (formulas) |
| 8D report PDF | quality topics | scorecards, the 8D steps, a ppm commitment |
| Delivery schedule XLSX | delivery and capacity topics | monthly quantities, lead time |
| Order confirmation PDF | at the deal | the agreed terms |

## Terms

Every term with € weight is a structured field. A term sheet carries **exactly** the case's
`negotiable` fields; `fixed_terms` hold the rest. Every negotiable field except `unit_price` takes
a value from `term_options` (or the supplier's standard value).

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `unit_price` | number, € with 2 decimals, per the part's `price_unit` | price |
| `payment_days` | int, 0-120 | days net |
| `lead_time_days` | int | order to delivery |
| `volume_per_year` | int | binding annual units |
| `contract_months` | int, 0-36 | 0 = a single order (counts as one year's lot) |
| `effective_date` | ISO date | from when the new price applies |
| `index_clause` | null or `{series, material_share, deadband_pct, base_month}` | the price follows an index |
| `incoterm` | `EXW`, `FCA`, `DAP` | freight per unit from the case file |
| `tooling_eur` | € | one-off |
| `ppm_commitment` | int | committed defect rate |
| `chargeback_eur_per_complaint` | € | what the supplier pays per complaint |

## Case file

Case files come through the API, not in the data package: `GET /v1/cases?set=practice|sandbox`
any time, `GET /v1/cases?set=final` wave by wave.

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `case_id`, `set`, `type` | `type`: `price_increase`, `renewal`, `rfq`, `bundling`, `raw_material`, `capacity`, `quality` |
| `title`, `briefing` | the situation, in prose |
| `trigger_doc` | the document that started it, e.g. the supplier's letter |
| `parts`, `suppliers` | what is negotiated, with whom (2-3 suppliers = an RFQ) |
| `negotiable`, `fixed_terms`, `term_options` | see [Terms](#terms) |
| `buyer` | your need and rates, below |
| `round_limit` | your messages per thread, default 10 |
| `refs` | data the case points to - a start, not the whole story |
| `facts` | hidden cases: facts that exist only in this case (e.g. a new letter), in the format of `facts.json`, citable in this case |

`buyer`:

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `need_per_year`, `horizon_years` | the need the deal should cover, and over how many years (≤ 3) |
| `current_unit_price` | what you pay until a new price takes effect |
| `fallback_unit_price` | what uncovered need costs (re-tender or spot, incl. switching) |
| `interest_rate`, `reference_payment_days` | your cost of money per year; your standard payment term |
| `need_lead_time_days`, `late_cost_per_day` | the lead time you need; € per day beyond it |
| `cost_per_defect` | € per defective part |
| `category_goal` | `stabilise` (strategic), `secure_supply` (bottleneck), `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - the company's category strategy for this part; the briefing says it in words, and the rates in this block follow it |
| `fallback_risk_pct` | % added to what uncovered need costs: buying it later is a risk |
| `index_risk_pct` | % of the indexed spend: the risk you carry with an index clause |
| `sustainable_margin_pct`, `relationship_eur_per_point` | `stabilise` and `secure_supply` only: the margin a healthy supplier needs, and € per margin point and year that a deal leaves it below |
| `freight_eur_per_unit` | `{EXW, FCA, DAP}` |
| `index_paths` | `{series: change}` - the expected index move over the horizon, `0.04` = +4% |
| `must_haves` | `[{field, op, value}]`, `op` one of `<=`, `>=`, `<`, `>`, `==`, `!=`; a deal that breaks one scores 0 |
| `alternative` | `{kind: none \| quote \| current_contract, ref, terms}` - what you get without a deal |

## Data IDs

IDs have the form `<type>:<id>[@period]`, are unique across the package and sit in the first
column of each table. `facts.json` in the package lists every citable ID with the values the arena
checks:

| ID | Fields |
|---|---|
| `idx:<series>@YYYY-MM` | `series`, `month`, `value` |
| `quote:` | `part`, `supplier`, `unit_price` (+ the quote's other terms) |
| `sc:<supplier>@YYYYQn` | `supplier`, `otd_pct`, `ppm` |
| `qn:` | `supplier`, `part`, `ppm` |
| `po:` | `supplier`, `part`, `unit_price` |
| `cost:<part>` | `part`, `unit_cost` |
| `fc:<part>@YYYY-MM` | `part`, `change_pct` |
| `news:` | `supplier` (or null) |
| `doc:` | `supplier`, `date`, `days` (notice given), `asked_price` (price letters) |
| `ctr:` | `supplier`, `days` (notice agreed) |

Offers made in the session are citable as `offer:` IDs.

"""Print per-case negotiation trajectories of a run: python traj.py RUN_ID [CASE] [-v]"""
import json
import sys

run = sys.argv[1]
only = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 and not sys.argv[2].startswith("-") else None
verbose = "-v" in sys.argv
d = json.load(open(f"/Users/linuspummer/Documents/coding/vibe_coding/munich-ehl-2026-final/.runs/{run}/report.json"))
scores = []
for c in d["cases"]:
    if only and not c["case_id"].endswith(only):
        continue
    scores.append(c.get("score") or 0)
    span = (c["c_open"] or 0) - (c["c_best"] or 0)
    print(f"== {c['case_id']} score={c.get('score')} rounds={c.get('rounds')} end={c.get('end_reason')} "
          f"open={c['c_open']:.0f} best={c['c_best']:.0f} deal={c.get('c_deal')} alt={c.get('c_alt')} sup={c.get('supplier_id')}")
    for t in c.get("trace") or []:
        m = t["move"]
        if t["actor"] == "buyer":
            sheets = [s["terms"] for s in m.get("term_sheets") or []]
            act = m.get("action")
            print(f"  r{t['round']} BUYER -> {m.get('supplier_id')} {act or ''} prices={[s.get('unit_price') for s in sheets]}")
            if verbose:
                for s in sheets:
                    print("      ", {k: v for k, v in s.items()})
                print("      ", (m.get("body") or "").replace("\n", " | ")[:1500])
        else:
            tt = m.get("terms") or {}
            alts = [a["terms"].get("unit_price") for a in m.get("alternatives") or []]
            print(f"  r{t['round']} {t['actor']} {m.get('status')} price={tt.get('unit_price')} alts={alts} cr={[x['result'] for x in m.get('claim_results') or []]}")
            if verbose:
                print("      ", tt)
                print("      ", (m.get("text") or "").replace("\n", " | ")[:1500])
if scores:
    print("mean", round(sum(scores) / len(scores), 4), "n", len(scores))

"""The published cost function: what a term sheet costs the buyer in €, plus term helpers.

C covers the buyer's fixed need over a fixed horizon: need the deal does not cover is bought at
the case's fallback price (plus the fallback risk of the category goal), committed volume is bought
needed or not, and units bought before a new price takes effect cost the current price. In
strategic and bottleneck cases a deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin costs
too - pass your estimate of the supplier (`supplier_value`) to price that. Do the arithmetic here,
not in the language model.
"""

import math
import operator
from datetime import date

# Strategic and bottleneck goals: leaving the supplier below a sustainable margin costs.
RELATIONSHIP_GOALS = {"stabilise", "secure_supply"}
OPS = {
    "<=": operator.le,
    "<": operator.lt,
    ">=": operator.ge,
    ">": operator.gt,
    "==": operator.eq,
    "!=": operator.ne,
}


def closing_terms(case, terms, standard=None):
    """The terms a deal would close on: the term sheet, then the supplier's standard terms (from
    its quote PDF) for anything left out, then the case's fixed terms; gaps from the buyer's plan.
    """
    b = case["buyer"]
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    plan = {
        "volume_per_year": b["need_per_year"],
        "contract_months": round(12 * b["horizon_years"]),
        "payment_days": b["reference_payment_days"],
        "lead_time_days": b["need_lead_time_days"],
        # an unknown Incoterm counts as the costliest: a cautious buyer does not assume DAP
        "incoterm": max(freight, key=freight.get),
    }
    t = dict(plan)
    for layer in (standard or {}, case.get("fixed_terms", {}), terms):
        t.update({k: v for k, v in layer.items() if v is not None or k not in plan})
    return t


def horizon_start(case):
    """The horizon starts at the fixed or the earliest possible effective date."""
    fixed = case.get("fixed_terms", {}).get("effective_date")
    options = [o for o in case.get("term_options", {}).get("effective_date", []) if o]
    first = fixed or (min(options) if options else None)
    return date.fromisoformat(first) if first else None


def _years(case, t):
    """Years of the horizon a deal covers; a single order (0 months) counts as one year's lot.
    A commitment beyond the horizon neither costs nor earns."""
    months = t["contract_months"]
    return min(months / 12 if months else 1.0, case["buyer"]["horizon_years"])


def _units_before(case, t, years):
    """Units bought between the horizon start and the date a new price takes effect."""
    start = horizon_start(case)
    if not t.get("effective_date") or start is None:
        return 0.0
    lag = (date.fromisoformat(t["effective_date"]) - start).days / 365
    return t["volume_per_year"] * min(max(lag, 0.0), years)


def supplier_value(case, terms, supplier):
    """What a deal is worth to the supplier per unit, in cash: the price at its standard terms that
    would pay it the same. `supplier` is your estimate of it:
      standard       its standard terms (quote PDF, `docs.standard_terms`)
      interest_rate  what money now is worth to it per year (more to a supplier short of cash)
      usual_rate     its usual cost of money (default: interest_rate); tooling paid up front is
                     worth more to it when cash is dearer than usual
      ppm            the defect rate it really achieves (default: its standard ppm commitment)
      extra          EUR per unit it gains (+) or spends (-) beyond these items, e.g. overtime for
                     a faster delivery or idle capacity a larger volume fills (default 0)
    Contract length and an index clause are security, not cash: they do not count here."""
    b, std = case["buyer"], {**supplier["standard"], **case.get("fixed_terms", {})}
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, std)
    years = _years(case, t)
    sold = t["volume_per_year"] * years
    old = _units_before(case, t, years) / sold  # sold at the current price
    rate = supplier["interest_rate"]
    pay = 1 - rate * (t["payment_days"] - std["payment_days"]) / 360
    cash_now = 1 + (rate - supplier.get("usual_rate", rate)) * years / 2
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    ppm = supplier.get("ppm", std.get("ppm_commitment") or 0)
    return (
        t["unit_price"] * (1 - old) * pay
        + old * (b.get("current_unit_price") or 0.0) * pay
        + freight[t["incoterm"]]
        - freight[std["incoterm"]]  # it carries the freight leg
        + ((t.get("tooling_eur") or 0) - (std.get("tooling_eur") or 0)) / sold * cash_now
        - ppm / 1e6 * ((t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0) - (std.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0))
        + supplier.get("extra", 0.0)
    )


def _soft(gap):
    """Margin points below the sustainable margin, as they cost: none above it, quadratic over
    the first 5 points, linear beyond - no kink."""
    if gap <= 0:
        return 0.0
    return gap * gap / 10 if gap <= 5 else gap - 2.5


def relationship_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None, value=None):
    """Strategic and bottleneck goals only: EUR for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier
    below `sustainable_margin_pct`, per year covered. `supplier["full_cost"]` (EUR per unit) is your
    estimate of its full cost; `value` overrides `supplier_value`. Without an estimate: 0."""
    b = case["buyer"]
    per_point, sustainable = b.get("relationship_eur_per_point"), b.get("sustainable_margin_pct")
    if b.get("category_goal") not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS or not per_point or not sustainable or not supplier:
        return 0.0
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    worth = value if value is not None else supplier_value(case, t, supplier)
    margin = (worth - supplier["full_cost"]) / worth * 100
    return per_point * _soft(sustainable - margin) * _years(case, t)


def cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C by part. `standard`: the supplier's standard terms for anything the term sheet leaves out.
    `supplier`: your estimate of the supplier for the relationship term (`supplier_value`)."""
    b, t = case["buyer"], closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    if t.get("unit_price") is None:
        raise ValueError("no unit_price: a term sheet without a price has no cost")
    years = _years(case, t)
    committed = t["volume_per_year"] * years  # bought, needed or not
    covered = min(t["volume_per_year"], b["need_per_year"]) * years
    pre = _units_before(case, t, years)
    at_new_price = (committed - pre) * t["unit_price"]
    spend = pre * (b.get("current_unit_price") or t["unit_price"]) + at_new_price
    per_defect = b.get("cost_per_defect", 0)
    defect_cost = per_defect - min(t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0, per_defect)
    index = index_risk = 0.0
    if clause := t.get("index_clause"):
        path = b.get("index_paths", {}).get(clause["series"], 0.0)
        moved = max(0.0, abs(path) - clause["deadband_pct"] / 100)
        index = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * moved * math.copysign(1, path)
        index_risk = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * b.get("index_risk_pct", 0) / 100
    uncovered = (b["need_per_year"] * b["horizon_years"] - covered) * b["fallback_unit_price"]
    need = b["need_lead_time_days"]
    return {
        "price": spend,
        "uncovered_need": uncovered,
        "fallback_risk": uncovered * b.get("fallback_risk_pct", 0) / 100,
        "payment_terms": spend * b["interest_rate"] * (b["reference_payment_days"] - t["payment_days"]) / 360,
        "freight": committed * b["freight_eur_per_unit"][t["incoterm"]],
        "late_delivery": b.get("late_cost_per_day", 0) * max(0, t["lead_time_days"] - need),
        "quality": committed * (t.get("ppm_commitment") or 0) / 1e6 * defect_cost,
        "tooling": t.get("tooling_eur") or 0.0,
        "index_clause": index,
        "index_risk": index_risk,
        "relationship": relationship_cost(case, t, supplier=supplier),
    }


def total_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C in EUR; infinite for terms without a price (e.g. a supplier that quotes none), so such a
    sheet is never the cheapest and never beats an alternative."""
    if closing_terms(case, terms, standard).get("unit_price") is None:
        return math.inf
    return round(sum(cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard, supplier).values()), 2)


def score(c_open, c_deal, c_best):
    if c_deal is None:
        return 0.0
    if c_open - c_best <= 0.01:  # no room to negotiate: matching the best is full marks
        return 1.0 if c_deal <= c_best + 0.01 else 0.0
    return min(1.0, max(0.0, (c_open - c_deal) / (c_open - c_best)))


def must_haves_ok(case, terms, standard=None):
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    for m in case["buyer"].get("must_haves", []):
        value = t.get(m["field"])
        if value is None and m["op"] not in ("==", "!="):
            return False
        if not OPS[m["op"]](value, m["value"]):
            return False
    return True


def snap(case, field, value):
    """The allowed value closest to `value` (case `term_options`), else `value` unchanged."""
    options = case.get("term_options", {}).get(field)
    if not options or value in options:
        return value
    if isinstance(value, int | float) and all(isinstance(o, int | float) for o in options):
        return min(options, key=lambda o: (abs(o - value), o))
    return options[0]


def complete_offer(case, terms):

"""Observer: one ledger per supplier thread - what it offers, how it moved, how our claims landed."""

import math

from arena_kit.docs import quote_terms, standard_terms
from arena_kit.harness.validation import acceptable
from arena_kit.harness.valuation import ranked_offers, value
from arena_kit.play import ENDED, latest, moves_left, standing

TEXT_CHARS = 1200
ATTACH_CHARS = 1500


def _quote_sections(events):
    """Sections of the first readable quote PDF in the thread (the opening offer)."""
    for msg in events:
        for att in msg.get("attachments") or []:
            if att.get("name", "").startswith("quote") and att.get("text"):
                try:
                    return quote_terms(att["text"])
                except Exception:
                    return {}
    return {}


def build(case, threads, models=None):
    out = {}
    for sid, events in threads.items():
        led = {"supplier_id": sid}
        try:
            last = latest(events)
        except StopIteration:
            continue
        offer_id, terms = standing(events)
        model = (models or {}).get(sid)
        ranked = ranked_offers(case, events, model)
        # Only the standing (first) sheet can be accepted; a cheaper alternative is mirrored back instead.
        primary = [s for s in ranked if s.get("primary", True)]
        eligible = [s for s in primary if s["beats_alternative"]]
        best = None
        if eligible or primary:
            best = (eligible or primary)[0]
            offer_id, terms = best["term_sheet_id"], best["terms"]
        alts = [s for s in ranked if not s.get("primary", True) and s["beats_alternative"]]
        led["alt_better"] = (
            {"term_sheet_id": alts[0]["term_sheet_id"], "terms": alts[0]["terms"], "cost": alts[0]["cost"]}
            if alts and best is not None and alts[0]["cost"] < best["cost"] - 1.0
            else None
        )
        led["offers"] = ranked
        led["model"] = model
        led.update(offer_id=offer_id, terms=terms, price=terms.get("unit_price"), status=last.get("status"))
        led["ended"] = last.get("status") in ENDED
        led["std"] = standard_terms(events)
        led["stated_open"] = _quote_sections(events).get("stated", {})
        try:
            valuation = value(case, terms, led["std"], model) if terms else {}
            c = valuation.get("cost", math.inf)
            led.update(
                known_cost=valuation.get("known_cost"), relationship_estimate=valuation.get("relationship_estimate")
            )
        except Exception:
            c = math.inf
        led["c"] = c if math.isfinite(c) else None
        supplier_msgs = [m for m in events if m.get("from") != "buyer"]
        buyer_msgs = [m for m in events if m.get("from") == "buyer"]
        led["prices"] = [(m.get("term_sheets") or [{}])[0].get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") for m in supplier_msgs]
        led["statuses"] = [m.get("status") for m in supplier_msgs]
        led["rounds"] = len(buyer_msgs)
        led["moves_left"] = moves_left(case, events)
        led["our_sheets"] = [[s.get("terms", {}) for s in m.get("term_sheets") or []] for m in buyer_msgs]
        led["missing_fields"] = last.get("missing_fields") or []
        led["claim_results"] = [r.get("result") for r in last.get("claim_results") or []]
        led["claims_total"] = {}
        for m in supplier_msgs:
            for r in m.get("claim_results") or []:
                led["claims_total"][r.get("result")] = led["claims_total"].get(r.get("result"), 0) + 1
        led["from"] = last.get("from")
        led["body"] = (last.get("body") or "")[:TEXT_CHARS]
        led["message_id"] = last.get("message_id")
        led["signals"] = last.get("signals") or {}
        prices = [p for p in led["prices"] if p]
        led["move_pct"] = round((prices[-2] - prices[-1]) / prices[-2] * 100, 2) if len(prices) >= 2 else None
        led["total_move_pct"] = round((prices[0] - prices[-1]) / prices[0] * 100, 2) if len(prices) >= 2 else 0.0
        first_final = next((i for i, s in enumerate(led["statuses"]) if s == "final_offer"), None)
        # supplier message i answers buyer message i-1 (message 0 is the opening quote)
        # only messages with term sheets push; a holding note without sheets does not
        led["pushes_after_final"] = (
            0 if first_final is None else sum(bool(m.get("term_sheets")) for m in buyer_msgs[first_final:])
        )
        led["attachments"] = [
            {"name": a.get("name"), "text": (a.get("text") or "")[:ATTACH_CHARS]}
            for a in last.get("attachments") or []
            if a.get("text") and not a.get("name", "").startswith("quote")
        ]
        led["breakdown"] = any(
            "breakdown" in (a.get("name") or "").lower() for m in supplier_msgs for a in m.get("attachments") or []
        )
        try:
            led["acceptable"] = bool(eligible) and not led["ended"] and acceptable(case, events, offer_id)
        except Exception:
            led["acceptable"] = False
        out[sid] = led
    return out


def digest(led):
    """Compact view for the prompt."""
    return {
        "status": led.get("status"),
        "from": led.get("from"),
        "standing_terms": led.get("terms"),
        "standing_cost_eur": led.get("c"),
        "known_cost_eur": led.get("known_cost"),
        "relationship_estimate_eur": led.get("relationship_estimate"),
        "supplier_cost_assumption": led.get("model"),
        "current_offers": led.get("offers"),
        "price_path": led.get("prices"),
        "status_path": led.get("statuses"),
        "our_messages": led.get("rounds"),
        "moves_left": led.get("moves_left"),
        "last_move_pct": led.get("move_pct"),
        "claims_last": led.get("claim_results"),
        "claims_total": led.get("claims_total"),
        "missing_fields": led.get("missing_fields"),
        "standard_terms": led.get("std"),
        "signals": led.get("signals"),
        "latest_email": led.get("body"),
        "attachments": led.get("attachments"),
    }

"""Prompts for the Negotiator, Strategist, Writer and Reflector, and their output checks."""

import json

from .priors import GENERAL

PROMPT_LIMIT = 60_000

ROLE = (
    "You are the lead buyer of Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, a German pump maker, negotiating by e-mail with "
    "industrial suppliers. Each supplier is a person with its own economics: read what moves it (its notes, "
    "history, news, quote remarks, latest e-mail) and find the trade it wants."
)

NUMBERS = (
    "Code has computed every number. MENU: valid term-sheet packages per supplier (mid, terms, c = our total "
    "cost in EUR, lower is better for us; saving = how much cheaper than its standing offer). Code sizes our "
    "move each round: 'step' packages all cost us about the same and differ only in what the supplier gets "
    "(payment, contract, index clause, quality terms) - offer the 2-3 that fit what this supplier values; "
    "'trade' (only after a final offer) is worth exactly as much to the supplier as its own offer but cheaper "
    "for us. Send 1-3 packages from ONE level as alternatives; every e-mail carries packages. CLAIMS: verified "
    "data arguments (cid, sentence); "
    "pick at most 3, only ones that fit this supplier. LESSONS: what earlier cases of this run taught us - follow "
    "them as uncertain hypotheses, never as causal facts. Supplier preferences are separate from cash value. "
    "Respect evidenced counterconditions and do not repeat declined or answered questions. "
    "You may add signals: [{field, values: [allowed values], evidence: verbatim span from the latest email}] "
    "and proposal: {non-price negotiable field: allowed value}. Code computes the proposal's price. "
    "A signal describes this supplier only; use an empty list when uncertain."
)

WRITING = (
    "Write plain, professional, concise e-mails (at most about 150 words) as the purchasing team. NEVER write "
    "digits, prices, percentages, dates or data IDs yourself: put {{CLAIM:Cn}} where a claim sentence goes, "
    "{{SHEETS}} where the packages go and {{QUESTIONS}} for your questions. Each placeholder stands on its own "
    "line, as a whole sentence or block - never inside a sentence of yours. Ask each question once: either in "
    "your text or in questions, not both. Address the person who signed the supplier's latest e-mail by name. "
    "Never mention urgency, budgets, deadlines, targets or whether we have alternatives. No threats. Close with "
    "'Best regards' and 'Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing'."
)

NEGOTIATOR_OUT = (
    'Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else: {"suppliers": {"<supplier_id>": {"read": "<what moves it, '
    '<=200 chars>", "tactic": "anchor|trade|probe|concede|close_push", "level": "step|trade", '
    '"sheet_ids": ["M1"], "claim_ids": ["C1"], "ask_breakdown": true, "questions": ["<=140 chars, no digits"], '
    '"tone": "warm|neutral|firm", "prediction": {"status": "open|final_offer|agreed|walked_away", '
    '"price_move_pct": 1.5, "note": "<=140 chars"}, "signals": [], "proposal": {}, '
    '"email": {"subject": "...", "body": "..."}}}}. '
    "Include every supplier listed under suppliers."
)

STRATEGIST_OUT = NEGOTIATOR_OUT.replace(', "email": {"subject": "...", "body": "..."}', "") + (
    ' Also add "plan": "<your plan for the next rounds, <=300 chars>" per supplier.'
)

WRITER_OUT = (
    'Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else: {"emails": {"<supplier_id>": {"subject": "...", "body": "..."}}}.'
)

REFLECTOR = (
    "You review a negotiation our buyer agent just closed, to teach the next cases of this run. Compare what "
    "we predicted with what the supplier did; note what was too aggressive or too soft, which arguments and "
    "levers coincided with changes, and any mistake (contradicted data, wasted rounds, ignored signals). "
    "Treat proposed explanations as hypotheses. Price moves and final scores do not establish causation. "
    'Reply with ONE JSON object: {"lessons": [{"scope_level": "global|case_type|goal|archetype|supplier", '
    '"scope_value": "<case type, goal, archetype or observed supplier ID; empty for global>", "polarity": "do|avoid", '
    '"lever": "price|payment_days|contract_months|incoterm|volume|claims|tone|closing|timing|other", '
    '"lesson": "<one actionable sentence, <=200 chars>"}], "supplier_reads": {"<supplier_id>": "<=200 chars"}, '
    '"feedback": {"<key of each lesson in lessons_used>": "held|failed"}}. '
    "Give 1-4 lessons that would transfer to OTHER suppliers of the same kind, not facts about this case only."
)
